findings.desc: concept-naming: DISPATCH_LEDGER_ESTIMATE_MODEL (value claude-code) reused as preflight estimate model for codex/gemini dispatches in runBoundedRealLeafDispatch (lattice-dispatch.ts:2008); preflight estimate records for hostKind=codex/gemini will carry model=claude-code, which is semantically wrong — a codex preflight should carry a codex/unknown model, not claude-code. A provider-specific constant or unknown is needed for the codex/gemini ledgerCtx.model.

CHK-003:adversarial:3 intent requires concurrent dispatch test (two codex runs in rapid succession, distinct correlations, no file corruption) but the bound evidence file (usage-ledger-codex-gemini-smoke.ts) contains no concurrent test -- the note itself acknowledges sequential dispatches only. The dispatch-smoke CHK-001 concurrent-preflights test is preflight-only and a different smoke, not bound to this intent. The concurrent ledger-append correctness at the runBoundedRealLeafDispatch level is untested. A real concurrent test with Promise.allSettled or two synchronous appends to the same ledger file is needed to satisfy this must-priority adversarial intent.

CHK-002:edge:2 (model=null -> fallback model id) and CHK-002:edge:3 (correlation=null -> mints fresh) are must-priority intents with evidence notes that only cite code-path analysis (no executing smoke assertion). The codex-gemini smoke passes null correlation to recordDispatchFinalForProvider only in the OFF-flag test (line 296-297) which asserts nothing was written, not that a null correlation correctly mints a fresh one and still records. CHK-002:edge:2 has no test at all passing model=null. These are thin but not blockers given the code paths are structurally simple and the surrounding tests exercise the functions heavily; advisory to add direct null-model and null-correlation assertions.

CHK-003:edge:3 verdict is audit_only (result=pass) but the literal intent -- providerReportedTotal equals the stub token counts -- is not satisfied. The honest note explains why: openai/gemini structurally never report cacheCreation, so summary.ts buckets every codex/gemini record as unknownCount rather than providerReportedTotal. What IS verified: per-record token counts are correct, estimateCount===0 (no double-count), and the WHY of the intent (supersede semantics eliminate the estimate) holds. The gap (cache-less-provider tokens excluded from aggregate total) is a known design limitation tracked as out-of-scope follow-up. Judged acceptable at advisory severity given the honest disclosure and follow-up tracking; not a blocker.
